claims.text: Role in VVC: recurrent VVC: first a longer induction, eg, fluconazole 100, 150 or 200 mg every third day for 3 doses (days 1, 4 and 7),
claims.quote: a longer duration of initial therapy (e.g., 7–14 days of topical therapy or a 100-mg, 150-mg, or 200-mg oral dose of fluconazole every third day for a total of 3 doses [days 1, 4, and 7]
claims.locator: Complicated Vulvovaginal Candidiasis › Recurrent Vulvovaginal Candidiasis › Treatment

claims.text: then fluconazole 100, 150 or 200 mg weekly for 6 months = the maintenance regimen;
claims.quote: Oral fluconazole (i.e., a 100-mg, 150-mg, or 200-mg dose) weekly for 6 months is the indicated maintenance regimen.
claims.locator: Complicated Vulvovaginal Candidiasis › Recurrent Vulvovaginal Candidiasis › Treatment

claims.text: uncomplicated VVC: fluconazole 150 mg PO single dose;
claims.quote: Fluconazole 150 mg orally in a single dose
claims.locator: Recommended Regimens for Vulvovaginal Candidiasis › Oral Agent

claims.text: severe VVC: 150 mg in two sequential doses (second dose 72 h after the first);
claims.quote: Either 7–14 days of topical azole or 150 mg of fluconazole in two sequential oral doses (second dose 72 hours after initial dose) is recommended.
claims.locator: Complicated Vulvovaginal Candidiasis › Severe Vulvovaginal Candidiasis

claims.text: pregnancy: ⍉ fluconazole (a single 150 mg dose might be linked to spontaneous abortion and congenital anomalies).
claims.quote: Epidemiologic studies indicate a single 150-mg dose of fluconazole might be associated with spontaneous abortion (1150) and congenital anomalies; therefore, it should not be used (1151).

claims.text: Fluconazole (Diflucan) label: vaginal candidiasis dose 150 mg PO single dose.
claims.quote: The recommended dosage of DIFLUCAN for vaginal candidiasis is 150 mg as a single oral dose.
claims.locator: Dosage and Administration › Single Dose › Vaginal candidiasis

claims.text: CI: hypersensitivity to fluconazole or excipients; QT-prolonging CYP3A4 substrates (eg, erythromycin, pimozide, quinidine).
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN (fluconazole) is contraindicated in patients who have shown hypersensitivity to fluconazole or to any of its excipients. There is no information regarding cross-hypersensitivity between fluconazole and other azole antifungal agents. Caution should be used in prescribing DIFLUCAN to patients with hypersensitivity to other azoles. Coadministration of other drugs known to prolong the QT interval and which are metabolized via the enzyme CYP3A4 such as erythromycin, pimozide, and quinidine are contraindicated in patients receiving fluconazole.

claims.text: Caution in liver dysfun: rare serious hepatotoxicity, incl deaths (mainly in pts w serious underlying dz).
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN should be administered with caution to patients with liver dysfunction. DIFLUCAN has been associated with rare cases of serious hepatic toxicity, including fatalities primarily in patients with serious underlying medical conditions.

claims.text: Rare QT prolongation and torsades reported;
claims.quote: During post-marketing surveillance, there have been rare cases of QT prolongation and torsade de pointes in patients taking fluconazole.

claims.text: hypokalemia and advanced HF ↑ the risk of life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias;
claims.quote: Patients with hypokalemia and advanced cardiac failure are at an increased risk for the occurrence of life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias and torsade de pointes.

Concomitant use of fluconazole and erythromycin has the potential to increase the risk of cardiotoxicity (prolonged QT interval, torsade de pointes) and consequently sudden heart death. This combination should be avoided.

claims.text: High-dose (400 to 800 mg/day) first-trimester exposure: case reports of distinct congenital anomalies.
claims.quote: Case reports describe a pattern of distinct congenital anomalies in infants exposed in utero to high dose maternal fluconazole (400 to 800 mg/day) during most or all of the first trimester.

claims.text: Single-dose tablet: more drug-related AEs than intravaginal agents (26% vs 16%).
claims.quote: The convenience and efficacy of the single dose oral tablet of fluconazole regimen for the treatment of vaginal yeast infections should be weighed against the acceptability of a higher incidence of drug related adverse events with DIFLUCAN (26%) versus intravaginal agents (16%) in U.S. comparative clinical studies.
